previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for acute worsening of chronic right hip and back pain, which began shortly after his last discharge. He presented with severe pain limiting mobility and elevated inflammatory markers, but no signs of infection. MRI confirmed active inflammation in the sacroiliac joints and a small right hip effusion with synovitis, consistent with an ankylosing spondylitis flare. He received a CT-guided steroid injection into the right sacroiliac joint, continued high-dose prednisone, and supportive pain management. Nausea from medications improved with ondansetron. His condition stabilized, and he was discharged home ambulatory with a walker, on a prednisone taper, Bactrim prophylaxis, and follow-up plans with rheumatology and chronic pain services.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Long term (current) use of systemic steroids

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  INJ/ASP MAJOR JT W/FLUORO

INDICATION:  ___ ankylosing spondylitis on Prednisone 60mg QD p/w persistent R
hip pain.  // 1. Rule out septic joint, 2. steroid injection

TECHNIQUE:  The procedure was supervised by Dr. ___,
the attending radiologist, who was present for the critical portions of the
procedure.

COMPARISON:  RIGHT HIP RADIOGRAPH ___ AND MRI PELVIS ___

PROCEDURE:  The risks, benefits, and alternatives were explained to the
patient and written informed consent obtained.

A pre-procedure timeout confirmed three patient identifiers.

Under fluoroscopic guidance, an appropriate spot was marked. The area was
prepared and draped in standard sterile fashion.

5 cc 1% Lidocaine was used to achieve local anesthesia. Under intermittent
fluoroscopic guidance, an 18-gauge spinal needle was advanced into the right  
hip joint and aspiration as attempted yielding no fluid.  The needle was
repositioned 3 times without successful aspiration.  Subsequently, appropriate
position was confirmed by the injection of a small amount of water soluble
contrast and then 10 cc of contrast and 5 cc of sterile saline was instilled
into the joint.  Re-aspiration was attempted, yielding less than 1 cc of
serosanguinous joint fluid.  Then a mixture of 3 cc of 0.25% bupivacaine and 2
cc of Kenalog was injected into the joint.

The needle was removed, hemostasis achieved, and a sterile bandage applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and left the department in stable
condition. There were no immediate complications or complaints.

FINDINGS: 

There are mild degenerative changes of the right hip joint.  Successful
intraarticular injection.  No acute fracture or dislocation.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Imaging Findings - Mild degenerative changes.
2.  Procedure - Technically successful re-aspiration and therapeutic injection
into the right hip joint.

I Dr. ___ personally supervised the Resident/Fellow
during the key components of the above procedure and I have reviewed and agree
with the Resident/Fellow findings/dictation.
